items.title: She wanted to stay home, but a Kuching father’s insistence saved her when their house fell into the river
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 4 — Isniah Daud was tending to her kuih stall with her three daughters when a neighbour called to tell her that their riverside house near Kampung Bintawa Tengah had collapsed into the river yesterday morning. The 42-year-old immediately left the stall, leaving her daughters to continue tending to it, and rushed home. Isniah said she had experienced an unexplained sense of unease shortly before the collapse.

items.title: Cost, reduced regional allowance deter doctors from Sabah, Sarawak postings
items.summary: Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK) spokesman Dr Muhammad Yassin said some doctors were even willing to reject offers of permanent appointments if they were posted to either state. He said permanent appointments were not offered regularly, and rejecting one could affect a doctor's career prospects. Doctors urged to weigh options Dr Muhammad said the issue needed attention as permanent appointments were not offered continuously to all contract doctors, with some receiving only one opportunity during their service.

items.title: Rescued once, stranded again: False killer whale dies at Sarawak beach
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 4 — A false killer whale died yesterday after becoming stranded twice along the Pueh coastline in Sematan. Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) general manager Abang Arabi Abang Aimran said the adult female marine mammal was initially rescued and released back into the sea with assistance from the Lundu/Sematan District Civil Defence Force, Royal Malaysia Police and members of the public. He said SFC subsequently carried out standard operating procedures for stranded marine animals and conducted a necropsy on the carcass.

items.title: Putrajaya Line train services delayed after power supply disrupted by cable theft
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Putrajaya Line train services are experiencing delays following a power supply disruption caused by cable theft, Rapid KL said. Feeder buses have been provided to assist affected passengers. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Magnitude 6.1, 5.9 quakes strike Indonesia's Sumba, Aceh
items.summary: JAKARTA: Two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.9 in magnitude struck Indonesia's Sumba Island and Aceh province respectively this morning, with tremors felt across several areas. The country's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said the magnitude 6.1 quake struck at 5.55am local time, with its epicentre at sea, about 14 kilometres southwest of Kodi in Southwest Sumba, East Nusa Tenggara province, at a depth of 10 kilometres. BMKG said tremors from the second quake were felt in several parts of Aceh, including Aceh Besar, Banda Aceh, West Aceh, South Aceh, Pidie Jaya, Bener Meriah, Nagan Raya and Central Aceh.

items.title: Did you feel that? MetMalaysia says 5.8 Sumatra quake could rattle western peninsular Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale was detected in North Sumatra, Indonesia, at 7.37am today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement today, said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 4.6 degrees north and 96.3 degrees east, at a depth of 30 kilometres (km), about 59km northeast of Meulaboh, Indonesia. “The tremors may be felt in the western states of peninsular Malaysia,” it said.

items.title: Three male students held over death of Form Four girl
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Three 16-year-old male students were arrested yesterday to assist investigations into the death of a Form Four girl whose body was found in a school hall in Yong Peng here. The three were detained several hours after the body of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was discovered at about 5.30pm. The three are students at the same school as the victim.

items.title: True meaning of a successful workplace
items.summary: A truly successful workplace is one where people can return home safely and in good health at the end of every working day. We must identify hazards, assess risks and control them before someone gets hurt. Management must provide leadership.

items.title: After shuttle chaos, Sepang circuit chief pitches in as F1 fans wait for buses after second race day
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 4 — Sepang International Circuit (SIC) chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif stepped in to help fans who had endured a long wait for shuttle buses following the second day of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) in Malaysia 2026 yesterday. Azhan Shafriman and his team were seen on the ground managing the crowd and distributing mineral water to fans waiting for buses, according to posts shared on social media. Another user, @nrfaofdiaries, praised Azhan for personally stepping in to assist fans.

items.title: 5.8-Magnitude earthquake strikes North Sumatra — MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale was detected in North Sumatra, Indonesia at 7.37am today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement today, said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 4.6 degrees north and 96.3 degrees east, at a depth of 30 kilometres (km), about 59 km northeast of Meulaboh, Indonesia. — BERNAMA © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ringgit expected to gain ground next week amid weaker US job data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to strengthen against the US dollar next week, trading in the range of RM4.07 to RM4.08, as weaker-than-expected US employment data could reinforce expectations that the US Federal Reserve might skip a rate hike this month. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid told Bernama that the latest US labour market data could weigh on the greenback and provide support for the ringgit. Mohd Afzanizam said the focus next week would be on the tabling of Malaysia's Budget 2027 on Oct 9, with market participants likely to assess the government's fiscal deficit target for 2027 and whether there would be any adjustment to this year's deficit target of 3.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).

items.title: Bursa Malaysia key index seen in the 1,620-1,650 range next week
items.summary: On the index board, the FBM Emas Index decreased 286.07 points to 12,170.57, the FBM Top 100 Index fell 285.78 points to 11,957.68, the FBM Emas Shariah Index shed 245.91 points to 12,060.32, the FBM ACE Index inched down 3.40 points to 5,529.46, and the FBM Mid 70 Index slid 362.98 points to 17,481.93. Weekly turnover firmed to 17.39 billion units worth RM14.42 billion from 17.11 billion units worth RM14.07 billion in the previous week. Main Market volume declined to 10.31 billion units valued at RM12.69 billion from 10.41 billion units valued at RM12.31 billion previously.

items.title: Husband and wife die, five others hurt in head-on crash with 4WD near Sibu roundabout
items.summary: Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) Zone 4 Sibu chief Andy Alie said the incident was reported at about 4.15pm, with firefighters from Sibu Jaya Fire and Rescue Station arriving at the scene at 4.22pm. He said the two victims in the car were found trapped and unconscious inside the vehicle. “Paramedics from Sibu Hospital later confirmed that both victims had succumbed to their injuries,” he said.

items.title: In latest lawsuit, family of Bandar Utama school murder victim alleges duty of care breaches by Putrajaya, 17 others
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The family of 16-year-old Yap Shing Xuen, who was fatally stabbed at a Bandar Utama secondary school last year, has claimed in a lawsuit that breaches of duty of care by the assailant’s parents, school authorities and government agencies contributed to her death. Among those named are the boy’s parents, the boy himself, and several school authorities, including his homeroom teacher, the school principal, and teachers responsible for counselling and student affairs. The family also named officers from the Petaling Utama district education office, the Selangor education department director, the director-general of education, the education minister, the registrar general of educational institutions and teachers, the director-general of health, the health minister, the women, family and community Development minister and the government of Malaysia.

items.title: WhatsApp location helps rescuers find two lost hikers in Penang Youth Park
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — Two men who lost their way while hiking in Youth Park near the Botanical Gardens here last evening have been found safe. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 6.11pm, after which eight personnel and a fire engine from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene. “Firefighters conducted a search and rescue (SAR) operation based on the location shared by the victims via WhatsApp, assisted by three police officers.

items.title: Loke finds upside in DAP setbacks as party navigates new political realities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 4 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has described the party’s recent electoral setbacks, including its defeat in Negeri Sembilan, as a “blessing in disguise”, saying the losses have exposed challenges faced by rival political blocs and could ultimately strengthen the party’s position. Speaking in an interview with The Straits Times , the transport minister said DAP remained optimistic despite a series of disappointing election results and growing dissatisfaction among parts of its traditional support base. Despite recent challenges, Loke expressed confidence that DAP could rebuild support and remain influential within the ruling coalition, arguing that cooperation and compromise would be necessary as Malaysia moves towards its next general election.

items.title: Anwar welcomes Bahrain investment as F1 brings Gulf ties into focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain and is ready to expand cooperation in various fields, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a post on X last night, Anwar said the cooperation would cover healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing. He said the areas were among those discussed during his meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, who is visiting Malaysia in conjunction with the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

items.title: Student found dead in school hall was top student, tipped for 9As, says classmate
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was among her school's top students and was seen as a strong candidate to score straight As in next year's Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), said her classmate. The classmate, who declined to be named, said Irene Sofiya was absent from an extra class yesterday, but her friends initially assumed she was unwell. "I only found out later that Irene Sofiya had not returned home.

items.title: Hammer attack leaves Marang man dead, sister injured while trying to intervene
items.summary: The victim, Mohd Nasir Ismail, 43, the eldest of nine siblings, succumbed to severe head injuries in the attack. “When he came inside, he saw Nasir covered in blood with severe head injuries,” she said when met at her residence in Kampung Tasek yesterday. Hasnah said her second child, Affendi, 42, who has a history of mental health issues, is suspected to be involved in the incident.

items.title: Johor police confirm investigating Yong Peng student’s death, public asked to refrain from spreading unverifiable information
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — Johor police have urged the public to give investigators space to conduct a thorough probe into the death of a female student at a secondary school in Yong Peng. Johor Deputy Police Chief Datuk M. Kumar said authorities are currently investigating the incident and called on the public to refrain from making speculations that could interfere with the investigation process. He said police are gathering information and examining all aspects of the case to determine the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.

items.title: School murder: Grandmother holds dying granddaughter, helps her recite the syahadah
items.summary: Her grandmother, Jameyah Rabani, 65, said Fiya's friend found her in a pool of blood and called for her to enter the hall. Jameyah said Fiya became unresponsive when she called her name several times. "Yesterday, Fiya attended an extra class from 2pm to about 5pm.

items.title: Protests over housing flare in Spain after relief measures rejected
items.summary: MADRID, (Spain): Tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities in Spain on Saturday to demand affordable housing, a day after lawmakers rejected relief measures for tenants. The defeat infuriated those protesting the country's increasingly expensive housing market. - General strike call - Earlier Saturday, demonstrators marched through the capital's streets.

items.title: Crash investigators check 800 motor cases yearly
items.summary: General Adjustment Expertise Sdn Bhd investigation manager Jegatheesan Balakrishnan said each investigator handles about 65 motor cases a month. Of these, eight to 10 cases involve false or exaggerated claims, he said. He said the cases included fraudulent or staged damage, ranging from simple "parked and damaged" incidents involving false police reports to complex, staged multi-vehicle collisions.

items.title: Fraudulent claims cannot justify higher premiums, say consumer groups
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Consumers should not be unfairly burdened due to fraudulent or manipulated motor insurance claims, the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) said. Fomca chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan said the reality was that rising claims costs would eventually affect insurance premiums. He said it was time to revamp the motor insurance claims ecosystem as the present framework clearly needed stronger checks and balances.

items.title: Police probe involving Caprice over alleged document disclosure now under DPP review
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — An investigation paper (IP) into a police report lodged by businessman Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan over the alleged disclosure of an official document is now under review by the Selangor Deputy Public Prosecutor’s Office. Jeyenderan’s lawyer, Muniandy Vestanathan, said his firm had received a letter dated Aug 28, 2026, signed by Selangor Criminal Investigation Department chief SAC Zulkarnain Samsudin, on the status of the investigation. The police investigation is separate from civil proceedings involving Jeyenderan and Ariz, which Muniandy said are scheduled to begin in February 2027 at the Kuala Lumpur High Court.

items.title: AI needs safety layers like nuclear plants - ex-OpenAI engineer
items.summary: NEW YORK: Another former OpenAI employee has added his voice to a chorus of frantic calls to make AI safe, saying the industry must mimic the aviation or nuclear power sectors with their layers of safeguards to avoid disaster. In an article published in The Atlantic Magazine, David Robinson echoed warnings from inside and outside the AI world that its agents are being developed so fast and becoming so smart they could soon elude control and conceivably wipe out humanity. Robinson said alarming incidents reported since the start of the summer – in which AI agents slipped out of their controlled spaces and went rogue to attack a variety of targets – show the industry is not taking safety nearly seriously enough as it sprints to develop faster and more powerful artificial intelligence capabilities.

items.title: Taman Sri Muda flood victims staying vigilant
items.summary: Thinash Kumar Nair, 43, a cybersecurity firm sales director who has lived in the area for 14 years, said the sight of his double-storey home being inundated was traumatic. Recalling the tragedy, Thinash said he lost all household contents, including furniture and electronics, and two vehicles. Another resident, Pirakas Sabapathy, 35, said his family lost about RM10,000.

items.title: RM1b lost yearly to fraud, say adjusters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fraudulent motor insurance claims account for an estimated RM1 billion in losses annually, said insurance adjusters. Foo said the most prevalent fraudulent claims involved accidents, vehicle thefts, fires and staged collisions. "While the majority of claims submitted to insurers are genuine, fraud remains a persistent issue," he said.

items.title: Storms, flooding cause chaos on Greek holiday island of Crete
items.summary: ATHENS: Floods after heavy storms trapped some people in their cars and forced the evacuation of some tourists on the Greek holiday island of Crete, local officials said Saturday. The force of the flooding washed some cars and trees into the sea. On the road between Ierapetra and Sitia, flooding trapped 23 people in their cars, state television channel ERT reported.

items.title: AI, digital forensics key tools to combat fake motor insurance claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian general insurers have deployed advanced digital forensics, artificial intelligence and centralised tracking databases to combat organised crime syndicates and fake claims. The General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM) said the Fraud Intelligence System (FIS), managed by Insurance Services Malaysia, serves as the industry's primary database, allowing subscribing insurance companies to identify anomalies in claims. Chua said major insurers saved RM65 million between 2023 and last year by deploying the FIS to intercept dubious claims before payouts were made.

items.title: Motor insurance fraud on the rise [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Motor insurance fraud cases have surged dramatically over the past three years, driven by evolving syndicate tactics, opportunistic financial schemes and the misuse of digital image manipulation tools to exploit claims processes. General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM) chief executive officer Chua Kim Soon said the motor insurance industry was operating at a loss as total premiums collected fall short of insurance costs. "As many as 10 per cent of all motor insurance claims filed with Malaysian insurers are potentially fraudulent or manipulated, resulting in financial losses of hundreds of millions of ringgit," he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH-Bersatu pact may boost chances against BN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A potential electoral cooperation between Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu could strengthen both parties' prospects in the Melaka election by helping the coalition shore up Malay support and giving Bersatu a broader platform. Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said the proposed cooperation could give PH a stronger platform to challenge BN, particularly as PH continued to face difficulties in securing Malay support. Mazlan said Bersatu could provide PH with more support among Malay voters, while PH could give Bersatu a platform to remain electorally competitive.

items.title: 16-year-old student found dead at Yong Peng school [WATCH]
items.summary: The victim was found by her grandmother, who went to the school after becoming concerned when her granddaughter had not returned home by about 5.30pm. A broken flowerpot was also found near the victim," the source said. Meanwhile, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said investigations were ongoing.

items.title: Full relocation allowance for doctors posted to Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry has approved full relocation allowances for medical officers posted to Sabah and Sarawak to support their welfare and facilitate cross-regional placements. In a statement today, the ministry said the approval was among its strategic initiatives to ensure financial constraints no longer burden health workers receiving postings across regions. "The Health Ministry has also secured approval for the same benefit to continue for 2026 appointments and beyond," it said.

items.title: Anti-vax posts weaponise Philippine inoculation fears
items.summary: WHEN Jenette Torres Odena's 3-year-old son fell ill days after receiving a jab as part of a Philippine vaccination drive, his photograph spread on Facebook alongside claims the inoculation had killed him. "I felt like crying," Odena said. The Department of Health said concerns about side effects accounted for 66 per cent of refusals and called misinformation spread by social media influencers a "major driver" of vaccine fear.

items.title: America's war machine needs a reload
items.summary: According to US officials, highly sophisticated cyberattacks were at the heart of operations earlier this year, firstly to capture Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and then to degrade Iranian sensors and communications in the US-led Operation Epic Fury. According to Lieutenant-General Christopher Eubank, head of US Army Cyber Command speaking at the same event, demand for direct US cyber support to wider military operations had been "constant" since the conflict with Iran began on Feb 28. The strain has also been telling on other parts of the US military.

items.title: NST Leader: Zetrix RM200m revenue lapse exposes urgent need for stronger RTD oversight'
items.summary: THE revelation that Zetrix AI Bhd, formerly known as MyEG Sdn Bhd, owes the Road Transport Department (RTD) more than RM200 million in unremitted collections is shocking. The e-government services pioneer, which has operated since 2000, collected payments on behalf of the Road Transport Department (RTD) for road tax, driving licences and traffic summonses. The Zetrix issue raises serious questions about RTD's financial controls, monitoring and accountability.

items.title: Three arrested after entering Kelantan through illegal jetty
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: A man and two women who had just returned from an entertainment trip in Sungai Golok were arrested after entering Kelantan through an illegal jetty here yesterday. Southeast Brigade General Operations Force commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the three Malaysians were arrested by a team from its Eighth Battalion about 7.30pm. "The three admitted they had visited an entertainment centre in Sungai Golok town.

items.title: Daughter finds 85-year-old mother dead in bushes behind house
items.summary: BACHOK: An 85-year-old woman was found dead in bushes behind her house in Kampung Pengkalan Baru here this afternoon. "Mother lived alone in the house. Hindun said her mother was active and enjoyed cleaning around the house.

items.title: Malaysia welcomes Bahrain investment, seeks wider cooperation, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain and is ready to expand cooperation in various fields, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a social media post tonight, Anwar said the cooperation would cover healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing. He said these were among the areas discussed during his meeting with Bahrain's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al-Khalifa, who is visiting Malaysia in conjunction with the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

items.title: Two hikers rescued after getting lost in Penang forest
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Two hikers were safely rescued after getting lost in the forest near Taman Belia, Botanical Garden, tonight. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 6.11pm. He said eight firefighters from the Bagan Jermal Fire and Rescue station, assisted by three policemen, were deployed for the search and rescue operation.

items.title: 'I didn't distance myself without reason': Ex-PJ MP on PKR exit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has rejected claims that he was absent from PKR affairs for more than a year, saying he became less active after an alleged corporate mafia issue he raised within the party was not acted upon. Lee, who announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP yesterday, said the claim that he had been "missing for more than a year" from party affairs was inaccurate and diverted attention from the reason for his reduced involvement. Yesterday, Lee announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP with immediate effect, following his three-year suspension from PKR.

items.title: Senior Citizens Bill to strengthen protection for older Malaysians, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 3 — The physical and mental well-being of senior citizens will be among the key areas addressed under the Senior Citizens Bill, which is expected to be tabled in the Cabinet soon, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said the bill was being drafted to ensure senior citizens receive adequate protection in various aspects of life, enabling them to enjoy a better quality of life. “The bill specifically focuses on safeguarding senior citizens so that they are protected in all aspects,” she told reporters after officiating the 2026 National-Level Senior Citizens Day celebration at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.

items.title: Anwar visits Sepang for F1 GP qualifying round, attends welcome dinner hosted by Bahrain crown prince
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix qualifying session at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), where he also inspected preparations and the overall running of the race. The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began yesterday with the first and second free practice sessions, followed by the third free practice session and qualifying today. In July, Formula 1 and the International Automobile Federation (FIA) confirmed that Malaysia would host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement involving F1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.

items.title: Malaysia aims for economic resilience over efficiency amid global uncertainties, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysia’s economic focus has shifted from pursuing efficiency to building greater resilience as the country continues to outperform growth forecasts despite global uncertainty, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said. Mida chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz said economic leadership also meant preparing Malaysia to seize clear opportunities while remaining resilient to unpredictable shocks. How many high-income jobs?

items.title: Anwar calls on young Malaysians to master AI and new tech to drive economic growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Malaysia’s youth to master emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing to drive economic growth. “Digital transformation requires AI. Otherwise, AI will master us,” he said.

items.title: PAS leaders missed Dr Hasmah’s funeral due to prior commitments, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said most PAS leaders could not attend Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali’s funeral because they had prior commitments at home and abroad. The party’s deputy president said PAS had conveyed its condolences directly to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family, according to Sinar Harian . PAS sent Muslimat wing chief and Central Committee member Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, and joined the tahlil at Dr Mahathir’s home, he said.

items.title: ‘Will my job still exist in 10 years’ time?’: Ahead of Budget 2027, youth minister sums up young Malaysians’ fears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysian youths today have three main concerns, including whether their existing jobs would still exist in the next decade, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said today. Speaking at the Perdana Fellows Alumni Association’s (PFAA) Youth Economic Forum 2026 (YEF 2026), Dr Taufiq said his ministry had been part of a Budget roadshow in six zones nationwide to engage with youths ahead of the government’s upcoming Budget 2027. “Firstly, can youths bear the cost of living?

items.title: Anwar’s nutmeg story: PM says grandmother’s childhood lesson on theft behind his anti-graft stance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he, as the prime minister, would not allow anyone to embezzle or steal money, recalling a lesson from his own childhood as he continued his firm stance against corruption in Malaysia. “But I said ‘Chinese farm’. And stealing is a sin,” he said.

items.title: Seeing parents pinned in the car on video call is what broke us, daughter says after Johor crash
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 3 — The daughter of a couple who died in a road crash at Kilometre 72.5 of Jalan Batu Pahat-Mersing yesterday never expected an incident she initially thought was minor to claim her parents’ lives. Ain Zanariah Mislan, 33, said she received news that her mother, Nor Azilah A Rahman, 49, and father, Mislan Osman, 54, had been killed after their car collided with a lorry while they were returning home from Endau, Mersing, after sending off her grandmother. Her husband, Mohd Hazerul, 33, then broke the news that her parents had died, while her two younger sisters, who were also in the Hyundai Matrix, were injured.

items.title: Anwar hints at Budget 2027 help for hungry university students, urges youth to lead now
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today hinted that Budget 2027 could include measures to help university students struggling to afford food, saying the government was already looking into the issue. Addressing thousands of youths at the Youth Economic Forum (YEF) 2026 here, Anwar said the government’s role included improving the quality of education and ensuring students could master Malay while strengthening their command of English and other languages. Anwar also stressed that young Malaysians should not see themselves merely as leaders of the future, but as leaders who could already work together to make a difference.

items.title: Sultan of Brunei arrives as Sepang hosts surprise F1 GP
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Oct 3 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which began yesterday. The special aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, landed safely at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Subang at 4.28pm. The Sepang International Circuit has been selected to host the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.

items.title: Manager held three more days over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
items.summary: The media previously reported that preliminary investigations found the suspect was believed to have manipulated approximately 480 company accounts using fraudulent documents between 2018 and this year. During the operation, the MACC seized 25 luxury vehicles estimated to be worth approximately RM25 million. The MACC also froze seven bank accounts, comprising four personal accounts and three company accounts, with a total value of approximately RM3 million.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to announce candidates in one or two weeks, says Amirudin
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 3 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election within the next one or two weeks, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. On September 27, Melaka PH confirmed that seat distribution among its component parties at the state level for the Melaka state election had been completed. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari was reported as saying that the final seat arrangement, however, would be concluded following discussions among the PH Presidential Council, state PH leadership, and Amirudin as PH election director.

items.title: Time for a review: Creative industry seeks more Budget 2027 support as TV production rates lag behind costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Creative industry players are calling on the government to maintain and enhance existing funds and incentives in the upcoming Budget 2027, while reviewing television programme production rates, which they say are no longer realistic amid rising costs. Malaysian Film Producers Association deputy president Datuk Dr Yusof Haslam said government incentives and assistance should be maintained without cuts to safeguard the sustainability of the local creative industry ecosystem. On the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI), Yusof said the initiative has not only succeeded in attracting international production companies but has also provided crucial support for large-scale patriotic productions such as ‘MALBATT: Misi Bakara’.

items.title: Malaysia cuts use of ozone-depleting HCFC by nearly 80pc, eyes full phase-out by 2030
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — The National World Ozone Day 2026 celebration has reinforced Malaysia’s commitment to protecting the ozone layer and tackling climate change through a transition towards more sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technologies. In a statement today, the Department of Environment (DOE) said the celebration, officiated by DOE Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon at a shopping centre here, carried the theme “Global Action for a Cooler Planet: Celebrating 10 Years of Sustainable Cooling under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol”. “Malaysia, which ratified the Montreal Protocol in 1989, completely phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and Halons in 2010.

items.title: Police arrest motorcyclist for riding against traffic, crashing into two KL marathon participants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A 21-year-old motorcyclist was arrested after allegedly riding against traffic and crashing into two participants of the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 along Jalan Munshi Abdullah early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at about 6.15am after the motorcyclist, who was carrying a 19-year-old pillion rider, allegedly passed through a road closure marked by cones. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.

items.title: Family of Bandar Utama school stabbing victim files civil suit against government agencies, boy and his parents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The mother and sister of the 16-year-old student who was fatally stabbed at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year have filed a civil suit at the Kuala Lumpur High Court. The family’s lawyer, Surendra Ananth, confirmed the suit that was filed on Thursday, adding that case management has been fixed for October 29. At the time, the family said it planned to pursue a civil suit as the criminal case moved to the appeal stage following the Shah Alam High Court’s decision to acquit the teenage accused on the grounds of unsoundness of mind.

items.title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling gets another 30 days in custody
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta in July over an alleged drug-smuggling operation remains in Indonesian custody after authorities extended his detention beyond the initial 60-day period. Harian Metro reported today that Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the extension was for another 30 days. “The Malaysian police were informed by the Indonesian narcotics authorities.

items.title: Sepang International Circuit working with partners, authorities to improve F1 traffic management
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 3 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is working closely with its transport partners and relevant authorities to strengthen traffic, shuttle and crowd management arrangements for the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) 2026 race. “The experience and safety of our fans remain our highest priority at Sepang International Circuit,” it said in a statement today. A Formula 1 driver is seen during the free practice session for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit October 2, 2026.
